proposed_comments.title: Bound worker cleanup after timeout or cancellation
proposed_comments.body: The timeout and cancellation paths call `TerminateAsync`, but this method waits for the worker to exit with `CancellationToken.None`. If the child remains stuck while its redirected pipes or cleanup path are blocked, the UI can hang indefinitely instead of honoring the advertised 30-second timeout. Bound the termination wait and pipe-drain cleanup, and return the documented timeout/failure result once that cleanup budget expires.

confidence.rationale: The current added termination path explicitly uses an uncancellable WaitForExitAsync, while the converged fork fixed this exact root cause with a bounded cleanup wait and bounded pipe draining.

proposed_comments.title: Restrict handles inherited by the worker process
proposed_comments.body: Using `ProcessStartInfo` with redirected standard streams does not by itself restrict every inheritable handle available to the child. A blocked worker can therefore retain unrelated caller handles, keeping resources alive and weakening the finite cleanup guarantee. Create the worker with an explicit inherited-handle list containing only stdin, stdout, and stderr (or an equivalent Windows handle-inheritance restriction), then keep the existing job-object cleanup around that process.

confidence.rationale: The current added ProcessStartInfo enables redirected child-process execution without an explicit handle allow-list, and the converged fork implemented PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST for this exact containment gap.
